sources.title: Nigel R. Dalziel: Pandyan Empire (2016)
sources.note: Publisher abstract directly indexed: later imperial phase from Sundara I (1216 to 1238), extent in South India, succession conflict and Delhi attacks from 1311. Abstract used, not unseen full chapter.

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri: The Pandyan Kingdom (1929)
sources.note: Tamil Digital Library original book downloaded. Image-only PDF visually inspected at printed 192 to 194,198,202 to 203,207 to 208,221. Printed 221 agricultural agreements; 192 to 193 Wassaf horse contract; 207 to 208 distinction between 1311 raid and later conquest. Older polemical terminology and claims about Indian horse-keeping deliberately not repeated.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: South Indian Inscriptions XXII, No.46 at Tirukkadaiyur
sources.note: Direct original edition summary, No.46 of Tirukkadaiyur, 10 September 1301. Communities fled disturbed conditions and later returned when the king resumed administration. The text describes prayer to the god, not a documented petition directly to the king. Mirror of official epigraphic publication; pooled with DHARMA SII22 grant under the same work.

sources.title: DHARMA: Grāmam temple land grant, SII 22.197
sources.note: Indexed original digital edition summary: Jatavarman Sundara I year fifteen, 1265 to 1266; nine and a half veli, remission of taxes, temple service instituted in king’s name by Vira Pandya. Full direct retrieval failed; only indexed summary used. Same underlying SII22 work as pdy-local.

sources.title: Michael Mitchiner: A Small Hoard of Chinese Cash Found in Gujarat (2008)
sources.note: Journal of the Oriental Numismatic Society 196,41 to 44; printed 42 directly read. The paragraph on Korkai/Kayal cites the author’s own museum inspection and earlier excavation. The Gujarat hoard is not attributed to Pandya territory. Only the southern ceramic evidence and 1279 Chola transition used; Polo material in the article excluded.

sources.title: Marco Polo: The Book of Ser Marco Polo, volume II, Yule and Cordier edition (1903)
sources.note: Book III chapters XVI to XVII, printed 331 to 344 directly inspected. Pearl divers, drinking customs and boys trading pearls are explicitly a traveller’s account of Maabar in the late thirteenth century. All new text is pooled with existing Yuan card’s Columbia excerpts of the same underlying work.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Epigraphia Indica XXIV, Srirangam inscription of Garudavahana-Bhatta
sources.note: Printed 91 to 95 indexed original and Jain Quantum transcription checked. Record B, 1257 Hoysala patronage, is distinguished from record A,1493 restoration. Hospital physician, assistant, attendants, medicine and paddy budget on printed95. Same-work mirrors jainqq.org/booktext/Epigraphia_Indica_Vol_24/032578 and ebharatisampat.in/pdfs/1696404782.pdf pooled here.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: South Indian Inscriptions XXVI, Later Pandyas
sources.note: Direct original-edition mirror read: No.544 fifteenth-century gopura poem, No.552 (1434) twelve paniyaram, No.561 (1462) collective temple assembly and festival, No.555 (1535) continuing Pandya ruler. Nos544 and552 calendrical/kinship uncertainties retained; exact day of 1434 gift omitted.

sources.title: Emmanuel Francis, DHARMA: Tenkasi gopura inscription of Alakan Kulasekhara
sources.note: Direct edition based on T. A. Gopinatha Rao, Travancore Archaeological Series I.6.5, printed159. Tamil scholarly Roman transliteration, line6 exact kulacēkara maṉṉaṉē; translation identifies King Kulasekhara. Summary allows brother or cousin for annalvi; no claim that precise relationship is settled. Fifteenth-century context corroborated by SII26 No544.

batchIdentityNotes.index: Exact indexed HB record1279 to 1492; no card or staged collision at claim. Earlier pandyas500 to 800 and pandya-state800 to 1000 are intentionally separate.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Three decoded polygons1279 to 1300,1300 to 1400,1400 to 1492, bbox approximately76.074E,8.027N,79.825E,11.445N. Public warning explicitly distinguishes narrow southern shape from larger thirteenth-century reach and later fragmented rule.
batchIdentityNotes.scope: Narrative contextualizes imperial revival before1279 and Tenkasi continuation beyond1492. Neither map endpoint is treated as dynasty founding/fall. Medicine paragraph is expressly Hoysala regional evidence, not a Pandya foundation. No sanitation or schooling invented.
batchIdentityNotes.sources: Manual work-level pooling required for SII22 introduction plus DHARMA grant; Marco Polo pooled with existing Yuan card excerpts. Same-work PDF mirrors of Sastri and EI24 not counted as independent authorities. No fell/successors override supplied.
